title: Prove necessary square-root degree growth for cyclic inverses (no κ)
body:
## Summary

A fixed positive circle gap cannot give a degree-independent cyclic inverse row-norm bound. This scoped mathematical proof constructs real dyadic exterior-root polynomials for every integer s>=0:

```text
d = 2^(2s+2)-1,  L = (d+1)(2s+7),  min_|z|<=1 |P_s(z)| >= 1/2
||1/P_s||_W               >= 1 + sqrt(d+1)/4
||P_s(Z_L)^(-1)||_infinity > 3/4 + sqrt(d+1)/4
```

The explicit finite witness length is O(d log(d+1)). The matrices still have Euclidean inverse norm at most two. The result rules out a constant degree multiplier; it does not prove the optimal growth rate. It adds only `research/cyclic-inverse-degree-floor/`, with the written proof, exact standalone verifier and source-bound metadata. No new kappa or supplier admission is claimed.

This contribution was produced by Nick Petalas. Credit Rafael Guevara / alephnan PR803 for the circle-gap inverse setting and unresolved degree factor, Ali Romman PR621 for the cyclic-kernel context, and Golay, Shapiro and Rudin for the classical flat-polynomial construction. Paul Balister's primary exposition is cited with locators. Older PR4914 and PR5080 are related fixed-quadratic and upper-constant results, not replay targets or executable dependencies. No global literature-priority claim is made for the classical methods.

## Evidence

- Before: PR803 supplies a sufficient degree-controlled bound and leaves degree optimality unresolved. Its exterior-root bound, later sharpened in PR5080, is linear in degree.
- After: the new all-parameter dyadic family proves necessary square-root growth, including an explicit finite cyclic transfer with every later Neumann term covered by the tail bound.
- Four exact coefficient certificates at degrees 3, 15, 63 and 255 check all pair autocorrelations, independent binary-adjacency signs, unaliased first blocks and complete polynomial residuals. The finite cyclic lengths are 28, 144, 704 and 3328.
- Sixty-five exact tail-parameter substitutions pass. A separate dense rational 28-equation solve, checked by literal cyclic convolution, gives inverse row norm exactly two. Seven invalid-input, identity, sign, direction and singularity controls reject.
- Warning-strict ordinary and optimized direct replays pass on CPython 3.12.15, taking 0.324 and 0.335 seconds locally. These are timeout measurements, not performance comparisons. Both emit identical generated receipts and source hashes. The registered runner passes both commands.
- Exact committed bytes, modes and declared source history pass for all six files at `a82e473263f3ebfbf841a0905d4fb0c5c8d08cda`. Official export and integrity checks pass. Ordinary and optimized replay also pass in a read-only Git-free export with empty PATH; all seven exported files, including the export manifest, retain their bytes and modes. AST compilation passes; no separate static analyzer is installed.

From the repository root, reproduce with the exact local interpreter path, or substitute another CPython 3.12 executable:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -X dev -I -B research/cyclic-inverse-degree-floor/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -X dev -I -O -B research/cyclic-inverse-degree-floor/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/cyclic-inverse-degree-floor
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/cyclic-inverse-degree-floor --check-source-history --check-modes
```

Expected scientific marker: `PASS_CYCLIC_INVERSE_DEGREE_FLOOR`. The verifier uses only the standard library, has no runtime predecessor inputs, writes no files and emits a generated JSON receipt bound to all six package files. Historical provenance is pinned to canonical main `7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a`. Main guidance and live overlap were refreshed before committing; sparse notes, arbitrary historical diffs and unpublished work remain coverage limits. [Advance CLAIM](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19361635).

## Limitations

The universal statement rests on the written proof; finite certificates corroborate it. The construction is not identified with a PR621 prime-power kernel and does not exclude stronger source-specific estimates. No optimal degree growth, coefficient-preparation algorithm, rounded recurrence, dirty restoration, tape/storage cost, complete caller, supplier admission or complete multiplication theorem is supplied. The selected frontier and all five framework assumptions remain unchanged. Lean, Docker and the selected cold replay were unrun. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed. No mathematical obligation was deferred solely to CI.

## Open next questions

1. Close the necessary square-root versus sufficient linear degree gap for exterior-root polynomials. Start with an upper estimate exploiting the absence of interior poles, or a lower family using more than the isolated first coefficient block. Neither matching step is supplied here.
2. Identify one actual prime-power cyclic kernel constraint that excludes this generic example, then carry any stronger estimate through a fully charged rounded consumer. Source-specific structure, preparation and the complete error recurrence remain blockers.

## Related open work

No open PR on the same circle-gap degree multiplier was found in the inspected live PR bodies, focused cyclic/Wiener searches and main README searches.

- PR6420 concerns separated circular Schur bandwidth and an exact periodic support family. It computes a different invariant and supplies no competing inverse-norm value.
- PR6411 concerns exact source-injection tariffs for observed partial cyclic echoes. Its call-price model does not compute this degree-dependent inverse norm. No extra predecessor computations were run for either comparison.

The completion refresh inspected this account's 13 other open PRs created since the CLAIM, PR6419 through PR6432 excluding this PR. None studies the same circle-gap degree multiplier or reports a competing value for this family. No additional scientific computations were run for that comparison.
